dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: The first order of drinks has been packed. It's for the aunt of the wife of Miss Margaret's cousin. This is the address...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? A fresh face — someone Paimon's never met before! Paimon wants to go with you and say hello!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: As you wish, Lady Paimon! I'll carry the drinks, and you can lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take it easy with all those drinks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't you worry about us! Paimon knows Mondstadt like the back of her hand... You just focus on mixing more drinks!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Looking at the address, this should be the place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, Paimon's in position, let's do this, Glenfidia!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: They ordered two cups of Golden Eden. I've prepared them according to the regular recipe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem! Paimon's here to deliver a pleasant surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Order number forty-three...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's brought the drinks you asked for, Glenfidia!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: One Scholar's Afternoon and one Stroke of Night, right?

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Let's see... Yes, absolutely perfect, Lady Paimon! You're even quicker than me when it comes to mixing drinks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's seen {NICKNAME} mix this one before! As long as Paimon follows {M#his}{F#her} lead, there's no way Paimon can mess it up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #But when it comes to flavor, Paimon doesn't think there's anyone in Teyvat who comes close to {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And speaking of not coming close... Paimon doubts there's a better drink deliverer than you anywhere in the world... It feels like every road's a shortcut.

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: You're too kind, Lady Paimon. Making deliveries is part of my job...

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: According to the latest training requirements, we have to race against time in full armor to deliver heavy supplies to each camp as quickly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Delivering a few drinks is easy by comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't realize being a knight in the Logistics Company was so tough...

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Everything went smoothly today, Lady Paimon! We can finish work early.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Amazing! The drinks stand delivery service has been a huge success!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If {NICKNAME} and Paimon decide to settle down in Mondstadt for a while, will we be able to order some drinks on delivery from you, too?

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: I would be more than happy to serve you both. However, I'm about to be transferred to Dornman Port to provide logistical support to our returning knights.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's exciting...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, we'll come visit you in Dornman Port!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Thanks for all your hard work, Lady Paimon. I feel so much more efficient now that I've had a little practice. I'm more than ready to take on the rest of the orders by myself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: I'm a fast learner. Besides, we're not getting such a crazy amount of orders right now — perhaps the novelty's already worn off.

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: I can handle most of the orders myself, and we shouldn't get rushed off our feet like before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Paimon thought she heard some passersby raving about the drinks stand! Paimon bets it'll be super famous soon!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: Thank you, Honorary Knight, Lady Paimon! We'll keep the drinks stand going from here on out. You can count on us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've got this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! You're doing a great job, Glenfidia!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From now on, let's call you... The Cocktail Knight! Next time we meet, Paimon bets your skills will be even better!

dialogues.speaker: Glenfidia
dialogues.text: What an excellent title... I'll wear it with pride!

dialogues.speaker: Helene
dialogues.text: Good day, my former clients... It's truly an honor to see you.

choices.text: What brings you here?

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Ah, we've had an outsourcing order. I've been assigned to Dornman Port to help maintain some precision instruments...

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: I've finished the job, but I'm a little too tired to head back to Fontaine right away.

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Getting the chance to try your drinks here in Mondstadt... I feel like I'm back up to 90% vitality already. I'm sure I could take on three times the work now without getting worn out!

choices.text: Sorry, uh, who are you again...?

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Just a freelance engineer, nothing special... Don't worry if I'm not ringing any bells.

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Once I find myself a steady job, maybe then I can earn a place in your memory!

choices.text: Give me a moment, I'll go fix you something to drink.

response.speaker: Helene
response.text: Alright, thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Valerina
dialogues.text: Ahaha, it's been a while, Cat Savior!

dialogues.speaker: Valerina
dialogues.text: That's not right... I should call you Honorary Knight in a setting like this.

choices.text: How have you been, Valerina?

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Hmm... Not quite perfect, but not far off!

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: At first, I had this grand plan... I was going to reopen Furball Fortress and kick off mass production of the Dodoco's Blow-Up-Erative Bomb-Nanza tabletop game.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: But then, an invitation from Natlan showed up and turned everything upside down.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Liliuo, the Frost Star of Ixquimilli, heard about my past achievements and specially invited my team to assist in exploring a complex ancient ruin...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: You know, she's a famous veteran warrior from Natlan. She only switched careers to become an adventurer after she retired from that intense pilgrimage thing...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: In only half a year, she's already completed a lot of S-rank Commissions and stands a real chance of becoming the next branch master of the Natlan Adventurers' Guild! Or at least the second-in-command!

choices.text: That name sounds familiar...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Who knows, maybe you'll cross paths one day. If you do, please give her my absolute best!

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Anyway, even though it delayed my plans a little, I'm truly honored to have been able to help Liliuo out.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Oh, and I made a pretty decent amount of Mora on the side too... My funding's looking better than ever!

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: All the teammates I brought along had an absolute blast and came back with great experiences. Like that one dancing over there — that's my combat chef.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Picked those moves up from the warriors in Natlan. Impressive, right? I'm thinking of teaching the cats back at the Fortress, too!

choices.text: This is the first I've heard of her...
Take a seat!

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: If you're busy, don't mind me! We'll have plenty of chances to chat later!

choices.text: Would you like a drink?

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: I'd love one! But if you're too busy, I'm more than happy to wait!

dialogues.speaker: Eija
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight! Eija Gretel, at your service! We can begin the flying demonstration and instruction challenge any time you like.

choices.text: Let's do this, then!

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Roger that! Vesper, put your best talon forward! Follow the Honorary Knight's instructions carefully.

response.speaker: Vesper
response.text: Shrawrr!

choices.text: Now that I think about it, how does a falcon conduct reconnaissance?

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: You're interested in the technical side of things? Wonderful! It's a little complicated, so I'll try to make things as simple as possible...

response.speaker: Vesper
response.text: Shrawrr!

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: To achieve air-to-ground communication, in addition to making the most of Amber's unparalleled reconnaissance expertise, we also integrated four different technologies...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Alchemical equipment from Mondstadt, Gardemek identification devices from Fontaine, principles for controlling overhead surveillance devices from Liyue, and expertise on beast taming from Sumeru.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Vesper has undergone special training. It's able to send over more than thirty simple signals to the mechanism on its back by using various tones and movements.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: These signals are then converted into a coded sequence of flashing lights, which are transmitted to the ground for operators like me to interpret.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Similar operational methods have already been field-tested on Liyue's overhead surveillance devices and used to eliminate multiple criminal syndicates and monster swarms. The methodology is proven and reliable.

choices.text: I think I've heard about this before...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Apparently, a big exhibition will be held in Nod-Krai soon, and a delegation from Liyue is planning to showcase some even more advanced technology... I'm going to go watch and learn!

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: However, for the time being, the flight instructions sent to Vesper will continue to use the same information chain that I detailed just now.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: From the ground, we transmit coded light signals. When the mechanism on Vesper's back receives them, it will emit specific tones to tell Vesper what to do.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: If the visibility is good, it takes less than a second from the moment the order is given for Vesper to react.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: But if Vesper can't receive the flashing light signals, it will rely on its memory and intuition to return to where it first took off.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Vesper's so clever!

response.speaker: Vesper
response.text: Shrawrr!

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Indeed. I became neighbors with Vesper when I was only as tall as the Spark Knight, and Vesper was only half as tall as me.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Of course, Miss Haniyyah's work, "An Introduction to the Principles of Beast Taming," also played a vital role.

choices.text: Haniyyah? I've heard that name before...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Hmm, perhaps you've met her before? I've only read her work, though I'd love to show my gratitude in person...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Right now, she's only released a limited run of proof copies, but her book includes a detailed discussion on communicating with animal companions that has benefited me greatly.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: If I hadn't found her work by chance at a small stall in Nod-Krai...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Who knows how many years it would've taken to realize our plans for air-based reconnaissance?

choices.text: Your rapport with Vesper is clearly a key factor!

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: That's true. It's not easy to find a bird of prey as clever and cooperative as Vesper.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: It's one of the biggest difficulties with trying to popularize a system like this going forward.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Still, I'm ready to take on the challenge. I'm going to study my beast-taming socks off — in addition to my regular duties, of course.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: And as the technology matures, perhaps the signaling equipment will become more compact. That way, birds like pigeons could become viable options, and the training process will become more standardized.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Just you wait, Honorary Knight!

choices.text: You and Vesper are obviously birds of a feather!
Does she have some sort of special insight in this area?
Is that even possible!?
What exactly does a Signals Officer do?

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Hmm... Do you know Phonia? She's the shining light of the original Signals Officers.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: It was Phonia who established our operating principles, combining incredible Alchemical technology with cutting-edge experimental tactics.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: She designed most of the training programs I completed — with the help of the Vice Captain and Leonore, our very first Signals Officer.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Then something unexpected must have happened. Once she finished compiling the signals handbook, she was transferred and took up a temporary role as an Intelligence Officer.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: By the time I got back from Dornman Port, Phonia had taken a leave of absence — I haven't been able to see her since...

choices.text: Actually, a few things happened...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Hmm... I get the impression it's a complicated situation... But the higher-ups haven't issued an incident report, so I guess that means someone like me doesn't need to know — I'm happy to leave it at that.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Based on what I know about Phonia, she'll be back in the game in no time. I respect her too much to think she needs any undue concern from me.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Shall we get back to the matter at hand?

choices.text: Good idea, I want to know more.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Alright! Let me think... We've already covered the operating principles — however, we've run into a few problems when putting them into practice...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: For example, echo and beam detection devices remain difficult both to operate and to maintain...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: An entire team of dedicated technicians would be needed to perform maintenance on the battlefield.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: These are precision instruments, after all.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: There's no way around it. This is the difference between theory and application.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Outfitting every unit with acoustic sensors or alchemical beam equipment isn't cost-effective. Mondstadt can't afford such technology at the moment.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Therefore, we have settled on two different paths — the first is to continue to tackle the key technical challenges.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: The second is to adopt the relatively simple optical-based methods that I've proposed.

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: The authorities in Liyue have extensive experience in this regard. I plan to keep in touch with Su Ding's team for regular guidance as development progresses...

choices.text: That's a lot to get my head around. Let's continue next time!

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Sure thing! We can leave it here for now! If you'd like to learn more about the relevant technology, I could probably write a short summary for you.

choices.text: I don't know what happened either...
I'll come back later...

response.speaker: Eija
response.text: Take care, Honorary Knight. Vesper and I will be ready for inspection whenever.

response.speaker: Vesper
response.text: Shrawrr!

dialogues.speaker: Dunkhas
dialogues.text: That Varka... He's even more formidable than ever...

dialogues.speaker: Elishka
dialogues.text: *hic*... I'm done... I'm never drinking with him again...

choices.text: Are you alright?

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: Don't worry, we're fine... Listen, kiddo, take this as a warning — don't ever try to outdrink the Grand Master. You won't win... I don't think he's even human!

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: Hey! Who are you calling "kiddo"!? This is the Honorary Knight — show some respect!

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: Oh-oh-oh-oh! My apologies — I'm not seeing straight right now. I didn't realize it was you, Honorary Knight.

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: ...In fairness, all I really said is that you have a youthful glow, and energy, and... affability.

choices.text: (There's something not quite right with these two... Maybe I should make an effort to be nice?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you two just returned to Mondstadt?

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: That's right, we recently got transferred back... We haven't been working under Little Lady Gunnhildr for long.

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: We've waited so long for a vacation, we thought we'd stop by and report to Varka!

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: We only planned to buy him a couple of drinks — just a sign of respect — but that old dog outmaneuvered us. We can hardly ask Little Lady Gunnhildr for the night off over something this...

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: ...Looking at it now, it's all pretty shameful. We really messed up!

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: We have to make this up to her! We'll help handle all the training reports tomorrow. That way, she'll have a third less work to worry about.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Little Lady Gunnhildr...?

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: Oh, I'm talking about the Acting Grand Master, Jean Gunnhildr — everyone feels at ease when she's around. She's the daughter of Lady Frederica!

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: It's quite sad to think about, actually...

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: Back when she was knee-high to a grasshopper, she'd stand outside the door to the headquarters, holding some test paper or other with a perfect score, waiting for Frederica to get off work...

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: Then one day, even Frederica thought there was no need to be any more strict about her written grades... What was it she said?

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: "It's okay to make mistakes every once in a while. You don't always need to get such high scores..."

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: "Otherwise, the other parents will make you an example to scold your friends. Cultivating a positive image in the hearts of your peers is something all knights need to be mindful of."

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: So, in her next round of exams, Little Lady Gunnhildr deliberately got one question wrong on every test. Just one question! Naturally, she was still top of the class, hahaha!

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: Ah... Where does the time go? It seems like only yesterday!

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: It really does... Hopefully, if we do our best to help handle the grunt work, in another couple of years, she might learn how to better conserve her energy...

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: By that time, us two old-timers'll be about ready to retire, haha...

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: With any luck, the youngsters coming through might possess half the drive and responsibility of Little Lady Gunnhildr!

choices.text: (Two drunken knights... Should I teach them a lesson?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Getting drunk at this hour! That's outrageous!

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: This hour... The day's still young, isn't it? We can probably fit in a couple more and still have time to sober up.

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: We just finished reporting to Varka on our situation since being transferred back... It hasn't been long!

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: But... Now that I think about it, Little Lady Gunnhildr is probably still hard at work.

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: Urgh, this doesn't sit well with me... We really messed up!

choices.text: (Best not to bother them...)

response.speaker: Elishka
response.text: *hic*... Remember, we need to do more to help Little Lady Gunnhildr tomorrow...

response.speaker: Dunkhas
response.text: I'll remember...

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: I haven't let my hair down like this in a long time... It's so fun!

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's hard to find time to rest these days. My mind and body are completely relaxed...

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: What are you gonna do with your house if we get stationed in Dornman Port? Are you gonna leave it empty?

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: I'm planning to rent it out. I've already asked someone to help me look for tenants. That way, we should be able to find somewhere a bit bigger to stay in Dornman Port.

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: And then when Leonore and the others come to stay, we won't have to squeeze in like sardines.

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: Great! And Dustball will have more space to run around in, too!

dialogues.speaker: Miles
dialogues.text: Hey, did you notice? It seems the Grand Master quite liked that gift we put together.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Great, great, great, great, great! That's wonderful, absolutely fantastic...

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Saving three months' salary to buy white iron chunks of the highest quality... then paying Charles and Wagner extra for their labor... It was totally worth it!

dialogues.speaker: Miles
dialogues.text: I contributed a tenth of that!

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: It was totally worth it for both of us! Round up the other twelve — our next meal is on me!

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: Still feel like it could've gone a bit further... The Acting Grand Master's sword pressure could've felt more imposing. Ideally, it would've felt as if a single slash could split a mountain in two, then it would truly live up to her name, the Lionfang Knight!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: From a morale standpoint, I agree. But in terms of presentation, I'd say the current level of artistic refinement is already more than enough.

dialogues.speaker: Horken
dialogues.text: When she agreed to let us put her image into the mini-game, I doubt she expected us to go this over the top.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What are you two chatting about?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh, perfect timing! Honorary Knight, Paimon, want to try out the Cavalry Company's "Knightly Play"?

choices.text: Why does it have "knightly" in the name?

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Basically, it's a kind of live combat experience, mixing Mondstadt-style costumes and sets with Fontaine's film tech.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Once you step onto the set, you'll fight powerful enemies and get a taste of that larger-than-life heroism you hear about in stories.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: As for the "knightly" part, in battle, once your faith reaches a certain point, you can summon a shadow of the Lionfang Knight.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: This will allow you to use "Dandelion Sword Pressure" to send waves of wind sweeping across the battlefield, felling evil foes like leaves scattering before a storm!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? The Lionfang Knight... Isn't that Jean...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds like you two really look up to her.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Haha, indeed. This project was originally meant to be a simple opportunity for friendly sparring. Returning knights need a chance to relax, but if they don't practice, they'll soon lose their edge in battle.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: But then Hedwig came up with the idea of adding "The Shadow of the Lionfang Knight" to spice things up a little bit. I thought it sounded fun, so I helped put in a few words from the sidelines.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: We really owe it to Captain Kaeya... The expedition's been away so long, I just wanted everyone to see how much stronger the Acting Grand Master has become.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Her administrative skills are flawless, and her combat skills have reached heights us regular knights can only dream of.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that's so thoughtful of you, Hedwig!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's super curious to know what "Dandelion Sword Pressure" looks like!

choices.text: Paimon and I want to try out this play!

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: I feel relieved knowing you two are here in the audience for our Knightly Play. If you'll just follow me over here...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I hope you enjoy the interactive performance!

choices.text: Let's witness the "Shadow of the Lionfang Knight" in action!
How's it different from a normal play?

dialogues.speaker: Hedwig
dialogues.text: Have you experienced the Knightly Play, Honorary Knight? Did you see Commander Gunnhil— sorry, the Acting Grand Master's heroic visage? I'd love to talk more about it with you!

choices.text: About the Shadow of the Lionfang Knight...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Impressive, isn't it? When it comes to swordsmanship, the Acting Grand Master is, to my mind, completely unmatched.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Captain Kaeya already knows this, but Horken probably doesn't. Before I was transferred away from the Cavalry Company, Commander Gunnhildr saved my life. Twice!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Back then, she wasn't the Acting Grand Master. Even though she was still young, she could already get the better of almost every other knight — even the grizzled veterans.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: But she couldn't beat that thrice-damned Inspector... The traitor, Eroch.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: ...Ugh, I'll admit it, he really was something else — a real dangerous opponent. He could hold his own against Commander Gunnhildr, going round after round without a backward step.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: If it had been me? Two strikes and I'd have been on the floor.

choices.text: I remember hearing something about this Inspector before...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: *sigh* People are complicated — the older knights say he wasn't a bad sort when he was first recruited.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Driven by a strong desire for wealth and power, he was corrupted and led astray — quietly involving himself in all sorts of unsavory schemes. His intelligence and skill at arms only compounded the danger he posed.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Anyone smart enough to match him in strategy usually had no hope of beating him in one-on-one combat. And those few commanders who could outmatch him blade to blade were often too busy with their official duties... which gave him all the room for maneuver he needed.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Thinking about it now — that sapphire ring he took as a bribe on its own was worth a whole year's wages for fifteen knights! Think of how many defense works or public projects that could've funded...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: And that smug, grating voice of his... Ugh, it makes my blood boil just thinking about it!

choices.text: Get a hold of yourself...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Right... right. Stay calm, Hedwig...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Thankfully, in their second official duel, Commander Gunnhildr dominated that slimeball!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Ha... No more than expected from Commander Gunnhildr... Acting Grand Master and the most formidable sword fighter of the Knights!

choices.text: What's done is done...
We've never heard of him, but you make him sound pretty dreadful...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: A villain wearing a mask of civility, that's my take. If this were an adventure story... He'd be the kind of dangerous, difficult-to-deal-with villain that turns up in the middle chapters.

choices.text: Why do you only ever call Jean by her surname?

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Because it's a name steeped in honor! For many knights my age, that name shaped us more than words can express!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: We grew up on stories of the Alder Knight. Inspired by her deeds, we strove to become Knights of Favonius, and were lucky enough to one day serve alongside the Lionfang Knight, giving our blood and sweat to Mondstadt's defense...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: It makes me feel like I could become part of a legend someday! I've been fortunate in this life — I can die in battle without regrets!

choices.text: Don't say things like that!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Haha, don't you worry about me. If this world works anything like a stage play, that sort of talk'll guarantee me a long and peaceful life...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: As soon as you make a loud declaration about dying a terrible death, the opposite is sure to happen. You'll see, I'll still be here when my hair's gone white.

choices.text: Could you not say something happier?
Let me give it another go...

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Sure, knock yourselves out!

dialogues.speaker: Horken
dialogues.text: Greetings, Honorary Knight. I'm Horken, Cavalry Company liaison to the General Affairs Company. Is there anything I can help you with besides the play?

choices.text: Tell me more about the General Affairs Company...

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Oh, so you're interested in the First Company? In that case, please allow me to give you a brief overview.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: The General Affairs Company is responsible for planning and organizing Mondstadt's general affairs — things like economic output, enforcement of regulations, city management — those sorts of things.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Because of that, most of their duties involve a lot of paperwork. As a liaison, my role is to assist Captain Kaeya in coordinating cooperation between the General Affairs Company and our own.

choices.text: Sounds like a pretty cozy position?

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: You're not wrong. The pay's good, the hours are reasonable, and most of the time I get to deal with the friendly, welcoming citizens of Mondstadt. It's a very enjoyable role.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: That said, if you have any friends who want to join the Knights of Favonius, it's probably best not to aim straight for the First Company.

choices.text: Why's that?

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: At present, we prioritize recruiting knights who've sustained combat injuries and can no longer serve at full strength on the front lines.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: As for full-time clerks, they're required to pass rigorous professional qualifying exams. It's fair to say that anyone training from a young age to become a Knight rarely has the time to study to that level of specialized knowledge.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Comfortable, well-paid positions are something you earn through proven ability and conviction. They're not easy roles to get...

choices.text: So, what's your situation?

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: My situation... isn't too bad. During an engagement with a pair of Eyes of the Storm, both of my legs were broken — compound fractures.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: After years of recovery, I can walk just fine, but I can no longer charge, much less fight shoulder to shoulder with my comrades. That's how I became a liaison.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you considered using prosthetics?

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Hmm... That's not a bad idea.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: If I could find a suitable model — and my comrades don't mind someone slightly weaker fighting beside them — I wouldn't mind trying it out.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: That way, even if that lunatic Hedwig ever returns to the frontlines, I'll at least be able to keep an eye on her — and spare my parents some worry.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Yes. Our families used to live one floor apart. When Hedwig was seven, her parents went abroad. After that, something must have happened, because there's been no word of them since.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: My family took her in. She stayed with us until she grew up, found work, and moved out on her own.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Even though we always treated her like one of the family, when a child's real parents are gone... often the emptiness that's left behind can't be filled by anything else.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: I think that may be why she so deeply admires Commander Gunnhildr — both of them.

choices.text: Deeply admires?

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: It's just a guess, really...

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: At first, she may have simply hoped that her mother was as brave as the Alder Knight, that her parents' long silence meant they were fighting some dark forces somewhere, rather than having met an unfortunate end.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: And she probably wished that she herself could become as strong as the Lionfang Knight — strong enough that one day, she could overcome every obstacle and travel abroad to find her parents.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Later on, influenced by the two Commanders Gunnhildr, she must have let go of some of those dreams. What remained was a single conviction — to fight for Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: That's why she pushed herself so hard to join the Knights of Favonius, why she threw herself into duty without regard for her own safety, doing everything she could to eliminate danger wherever it appeared.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: As her "younger brother," I figured I should do something to keep her from getting herself killed. So, I followed her into service with the Knights.

choices.text: When you put it like that...

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Well, I've gone on long enough. Thank you for listening so patiently. It's truly an honor.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: If you'd like to know more about the General Affairs Company, feel free to come by another time. I can prepare some documents and go over everything in detail.

choices.text: I still don't quite get it...
I'm not quite following the logic here...
What's Hedwig's situation...?

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Her situation is a little different... She transferred directly from the Cavalry Company to the General Affairs Company.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Her unit discovered two inactive Ruin Guards concealed in the bushes next to a major road. While attempting to neutralize the threat, the Ruin Guards suddenly reactivated.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: She and two comrades covered the unit's retreat, sent word for reinforcements, and held their ground until Commander Gunnhildr arrived.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: It took over a year for her comrades to recover, but Hedwig returned to duty after just three months. She was determined to eliminate the threat completely, so she returned to investigate the area where the Ruin Guards had been.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: This led her to a small and extremely dangerous Domain. Another brutal fight ensued, one that required Commander Gunnhildr's intervention yet again.

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: This time, half her internal organs were damaged beyond use. The fact she survived at all was a miracle. She'll need at least another five years to recover. The honors and rewards she received are scant recompense for the pain it caused my parents.

choices.text: So your parents know Hedwig, too?
Sounds like you two are pretty close...
Are there too few openings?
It doesn't look like your duties are stressing you out.
Alright then. See you around!

response.speaker: Horken
response.text: Take care.
